findings.claim: Required Practical 7 involves investigating the effect of a factor on human reaction time.
findings.truth: Reaction time is required practical activity 6 in this qualification. Required practical 7 is measuring the population size of a common species using sampling techniques.
findings.evidence: spec 10.2.6 and 10.2.7; spec 4.5.2 names required practical activity 6 as the reaction-time investigation

findings.claim: Different regions of the brain have different functions: the cerebral cortex (consciousness, thought, memory), the cerebellum (balance and coordination) and the medulla (unconscious activities like breathing and heart rate).
findings.truth: The named brain regions are separate GCSE Biology only. This spec names the brain only as a coordination centre and as part of the central nervous system; it never asks for regions of the brain. Two flashcards in the same lesson (cerebellum, medulla) teach the same out-of-scope material; they are left in place because the content now carries the scope label.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.1 and 4.5.2; grep of the spec for 'cerebral', 'cerebellum' and 'medulla' returns nothing

findings.claim: Question 4: 'Explain the role of negative feedback in homeostasis, using body temperature as an example', with 'triggers effectors to cool the body, e.g. sweating' in the key.
findings.truth: Negative feedback appears in this spec only inside Higher-tier-only statements (glucagon, thyroxine), and the mechanism of temperature control (sweating, vasodilation) is separate GCSE Biology only. Body temperature itself is named in the core list of conditions homeostasis controls, and homeostasis cannot be taught without the idea of reversing a change, so this is not worth an edit. Recorded so the tier question is visible.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.1 (body temperature in the core list); spec 4.5.3.2 and 4.5.3.6 (negative feedback, both HT only); no thermoregulation section in this spec

findings.claim: Question 4 asks the student to explain the interactions between oestrogen and the pituitary hormones during the menstrual cycle, with no Higher-tier flag. The same interaction detail sits unflagged in the hormone list in the content.
findings.truth: Explaining the interactions of FSH, oestrogen, LH and progesterone is Higher tier only in this spec. The lesson already handles tier correctly elsewhere: the menstrual-cycle key fact and the whole fertility-treatment section are wrapped in higher-only divs. The options are (a) leave it, (b) wrap the interaction sentence in a higher-only div and prefix the question text with 'Higher tier', or (c) drop the question. Recommendation: (b), but it changes question text in a data shape that has no tier field, so it needs Tom's call and would apply fleet-wide.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.3 '(HT only) Students should be able to explain the interactions of FSH, oestrogen, LH and progesterone, in the control of the menstrual cycle'

findings.claim: Many plants and some animals (e.g. bacteria, starfish) can reproduce asexually.
findings.truth: Bacteria are not animals. The sentence puts them inside 'some animals', which teaches a classification error in a unit that goes on to teach the three-domain system (Archaea, Bacteria, Eukaryota).
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.4 Classification of living organisms; settled fact

findings.claim: Question 4's key credits 'Each gene contains a specific sequence of bases / nucleotides (1)'.
findings.truth: Bases and nucleotides are separate GCSE Biology only. This spec stops at 'a gene codes for a particular sequence of amino acids'. The point is not wrong and a student would still be credited for it, so no edit; recorded because it is one of four credit points in a four-mark question.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.3 DNA and the genome

findings.claim: A higher-only div opens before the Punnett-square heading and closes at the end of the lesson, so Punnett squares, cystic fibrosis, polydactyly, embryo screening and sex determination are all inside it.
findings.truth: None of that is Higher tier only. Completing a Punnett square, inherited disorders and sex determination are core content for both tiers; only constructing a genetic cross to make probability predictions is HT only. Because css/style.css hides .higher-only under body.tier-foundation, a Foundation student saw none of this content while still being asked all six practice questions about it. The wrapper is removed.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.4 (only the 'construct a genetic cross by Punnett square diagram' statement is HT only), 4.6.1.5 Inherited disorders, 4.6.1.6 Sex determination - none flagged HT; css/style.css 'body.tier-foundation .higher-only { display: none !important; }'

findings.claim: Evidence for evolution comes from fossils, antibiotic-resistant bacteria and comparative anatomy.
findings.truth: This spec limits the evidence for evolution to fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria. Comparative anatomy is true science but is not in this qualification, and the lesson presents it as one of three things to learn (it is also in a key fact, a knowledge check and a flashcard). Not wrong, so no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.3.1 'describe the evidence for evolution including fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria'

findings.claim: All six practice questions read 'Cannot generate practice questions without specification content', with mark schemes reading 'Content requirements not available'. Two are labelled '9 marks - Evaluate' and '12 marks - Extended'.
findings.truth: The lesson shipped with a generation failure. There is no practice at all, and this qualification never sets a 9-mark or 12-mark question: each paper is 70 marks of multiple choice, structured, closed short answer and open response, with extended response topping out at 6 marks. Six replacement questions have been written on in-scope content (genetic engineering, GM crops, competition and interdependence).
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Biology Paper 2: 1 hour 15 minutes, 70 marks, Foundation and Higher); spec 4.6.2.4 and 4.7.1.1

findings.claim: Covers genetic engineering (4.6.4), benefits and risks of genetic engineering, ecosystems and com...
findings.truth: A truncated generation-failure placeholder. It also cites the wrong spec section: genetic engineering is 4.6.2.4 in this spec, while 4.6.4 is Classification of living organisms.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.2.4 Genetic engineering; spec 4.6.4 Classification of living organisms

findings.claim: Key takeaways: 'Complete specification content needed for accurate lesson generation', 'Genetic engineering and ecology are interconnected topics in modern biology', 'Exam questions require specific examples and balanced evaluation'.
findings.truth: The same generation failure. None of the three takeaways states anything the student can revise. Replaced with three takeaways drawn from the lesson body.
findings.evidence: internal: the takeaways do not correspond to the lesson content

findings.claim: A higher-only div (badged 'Higher Tier' on the page) wraps the paragraph on energy loss between trophic levels and the four-to-five-level limit on food chains.
findings.truth: Energy transfer between trophic levels is separate GCSE Biology only, not Higher-tier Combined Science. Badging it 'Higher Tier' tells a Higher Combined student it is examinable. The wrapper is removed and a plain scope sentence added. The numbered trophic levels earlier in the lesson are the same out-of-scope idea; this spec names producers and primary, secondary and tertiary consumers but never uses trophic levels or pyramids of biomass (see F15).
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'trophic' and 'pyramid of biomass' returns nothing; spec 4.7.2.1 names producers and primary/secondary/tertiary consumers only

findings.claim: For separate biology, you need to know the functions of the main brain regions and how scientists study them. Description: 'How the brain controls body functions, how the eye focuses light, and thermoregulation.'
findings.truth: The scope warning must be plain and must appear in the description too, so a student browsing the unit knows before opening the lesson.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5 has no brain, eye or temperature-control content

findings.claim: The whole lesson: regions of the brain, methods of studying the brain, the structure of the eye, accommodation, myopia and hyperopia, and thermoregulation.
findings.truth: None of it is in this qualification. The spec has no brain section, no eye section and no temperature-control section; 4.5 runs Homeostasis, The human nervous system, and Hormonal coordination only. The lesson half-flags itself once ('For separate biology, you need to know...') and then teaches everything as if examinable. Options: retire the lesson from this board, or keep it as clearly labelled separate-Biology background. The edits take the second option; the structural decision is Tom's.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.1 to 4.5.3.6; grep of the spec for 'cerebral', 'retina', 'accommodation', 'myopia', 'vasodilation' returns nothing

findings.claim: The lesson opens straight into the kidney with no scope statement, and the description reads 'How the kidney filters blood, maintains water balance, and how plant hormones work.'
findings.truth: A plain separate-Biology label is needed in the first paragraph and in the description.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5 has no excretion or plant-hormone content

findings.claim: The whole lesson: the nephron, filtration and selective reabsorption, dialysis and transplants, ADH and water balance, auxins, gibberellins and ethene.
findings.truth: None of it is in this qualification, and the lesson gives the student no warning at all. Same two options as lesson 9; the edits label it.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'nephron', 'kidney' (only a passing mention of urea excretion under diffusion), 'auxin', 'gibberellin' and 'ethene' finds no such content

findings.claim: The lesson opens with nucleotides and bases and gives no scope statement; the description reads 'The structure of DNA, genetic engineering, cloning techniques, and key discoveries.'
findings.truth: The label must say which part is Combined Science (genetic engineering, Higher tier) and which is separate Biology only.

findings.claim: DNA in nucleotide detail, complementary base pairing, triplets, transcription and translation, cloning (tissue culture and adult cell cloning) and the history of genetics (Mendel, Watson and Crick, Franklin).
findings.truth: All separate GCSE Biology only. This spec's DNA statement stops at 'DNA is a polymer made up of two strands forming a double helix' and 'a gene codes for a particular sequence of amino acids'; there is no protein synthesis, no cloning and no history-of-genetics section. The genetic-engineering part of the lesson IS in this qualification and is correctly wrapped in a higher-only div, so the lesson is mixed and should be labelled rather than retired. Structural call is Tom's.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.3 DNA and the genome; spec 4.6.2.4 Genetic engineering (HT only steps); grep for 'nucleotide', 'transcription', 'tissue culture' and 'Mendel' returns nothing

findings.claim: The lesson teaches trophic levels as examinable content with no scope statement; the description reads 'How energy and biomass flow through food chains, and why transfer is inefficient.'
findings.truth: A plain separate-Biology label is needed in the first paragraph and in the description.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.2 has no trophic-level or biomass-transfer content

findings.claim: Question 1 'Name the trophic level occupied by producers' has the mark scheme 'Trophic Lower band (1 mark).'
findings.truth: The answer key is corrupted: a band-ladder search and replace turned 'Trophic Level 1' into 'Trophic Lower band', so the question has no usable answer. The answer is trophic level 1. Written in lower case so it does not trip the house band-name rule.
findings.evidence: internal: the lesson's own key fact and knowledge check both give trophic level 1 = producers

findings.claim: For every 100 kJ of energy in grain, approximately 10 kJ reaches a human who eats the animal that ate the grain - but approximately 10-20 kJ reaches a human who eats the grain directly.
findings.truth: The second figure is wrong and it destroys the point of the key fact. At roughly 10% transfer, about 10 kJ of the 100 kJ reaches a human who eats the animal, while a human who eats the grain directly gets most of the 100 kJ. As written, eating grain looks only marginally better than eating meat. NOTE: the same wrong figure is repeated inside this box's data-revision-tip, which the raw dump truncates, so that attribute needs a separate manual fix.
findings.evidence: recomputation from the lesson's own 10% transfer figure: 100 kJ -> about 10 kJ at the next trophic level; eating at the lower level skips that loss

findings.claim: primary consumers: 'A primary consumer, feeding at trophic level 2, which is the most energy-efficient way for humans to obtain food.'
findings.truth: The definition defines the term with itself and then swaps in a claim about human diet, which is not what a primary consumer is.
findings.evidence: internal: circular definition

findings.claim: The whole lesson: numbered trophic levels, pyramids of biomass, the 10% transfer figure, the efficiency-of-transfer calculation, and intensive farming.
findings.truth: None of it is in this qualification. This spec's ecology content stops at food chains, producers and consumers, predator-prey cycles, the carbon and water cycles, and biodiversity. Same two options; the edits label it.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'trophic', 'pyramid of biomass' and 'biomass transfer' returns nothing; spec 4.7.2.1 and 4.7.2.2

findings.claim: The lesson teaches decomposition rates, food security and biotechnology as examinable content with no scope statement; the description reads 'How decomposition recycles nutrients, threats to food security, and uses of biotechnology.'
findings.truth: A plain separate-Biology label is needed in the first paragraph and in the description.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7 has no decay-rate, food-security or biotechnology content

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Required Practical: Investigating Decomposition', followed by 'You may be asked to describe an investigation into the effect of temperature on the rate of decomposition.'
findings.truth: There is no decomposition required practical in this qualification. The biology required practicals here are microscopy, osmosis, food tests, the effect of pH on amylase, light intensity and photosynthesis, human reaction time, and population sampling. The decay practical belongs to separate GCSE Biology. The lipase and cresol-red method described is left alone: it matches the separate-Biology practical and is not something this checker should second-guess.

findings.claim: the global population is expected to reach 10 billion by 2050 (repeated in the stem of practice question 6).
findings.truth: The UN projection for 2050 is about 9.7 billion. World population is not projected to reach 10 billion until the 2060s, peaking near 10.3 billion around 2084.
findings.evidence: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via Wikipedia, Projections of population growth

findings.claim: Question 1 'Name two factors that affect the rate of decomposition' is labelled '1 mark - Recall' and the key reads '1 mark for two correct'.
findings.truth: A one-mark item should ask for one thing. The question is changed to ask for one factor so the stem, the mark total and the key agree, and the lesson keeps its 1/2/2/3/4/6 ladder.
findings.evidence: internal inconsistency in the item; spec 2.2 question types

findings.claim: The whole lesson: factors affecting the rate of decay, a decay required practical, food security, mycoprotein and Quorn, biological control and hydroponics.
findings.truth: None of it is in this qualification. Same two options as lessons 9 to 12; the edits label it.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'food security', 'mycoprotein', 'hydroponics' and 'biological control' returns nothing; the biology required practicals are 10.2.1 to 10.2.7 only

summary: Board anchors verified in the spec: six papers, each 1 hour 15 minutes, 70 marks, Foundation and Higher; Biology Paper 2 = topics 5-7; required practicals 6 (reaction time) and 7 (population sampling). Five of the thirteen lessons (9 to 13) are wholly separate GCSE Biology - the brain and eye and thermoregulation, the kidney and plant hormones, DNA structure and cloning and the history of genetics, trophic levels and biomass transfer, and decay and food security and biotechnology. They are labelled, not deleted; retiring them is Tom's call. Two defects are worse than scope: lesson 7 shipped with all six practice questions and all three takeaways as generation-failure placeholders, and lesson 5 wrapped core both-tier content (Punnett squares, cystic fibrosis, polydactyly, embryo screening, sex determination) in a higher-only div, so Foundation students saw none of it while still being asked about it. Also fixed: a swapped required-practical number, bacteria called animals, a corrupted answer key ('Trophic Lower band'), a biomass figure that inverted its own point, and a 10 billion by 2050 population claim.
